title: Taking cut of the money thrown at T-Bone Walker
summary: As show director Cobb gathered the money thrown at T-Bone, who gambled it away in crap games, so he pocketed some for himself.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: What did you tell me a little while ago about you used to pick up the money that they were throwing at T-Bone?

All right. T-Bone would get on the show and they'd throw all kinds -- twenty-dollar bills, I was pretty honest -- boy from Texas -- on me, and I took up the change and the bills every day and I'd meet him backstage and I was director of the show, and give him all his money; he'd give me ten dollars, which was good. I mean, I'm doing this every show. But he'd go upstairs
and blew all the money in a crap game with Charlie Glenn and Joe Ziggy Johnson and I found this out and I said, "No kiddin'".

So I started taking me some money, Helen. So I was making off of T-Bone. He'd lay down with me some good money — I'd hang out in the evening and put that guitar and make that lickety-split, "In the evening, baby when the sun goes down, doo doo doo, and they'd scream "Wow" and throw that money down there ... from the balcony and everywhere.

And he'd go up and gamble it and tell Louie, and I'd say, "I'm not gambling nothing, I'm gonna take some of this money." And I'd give him his money and he'd still give me ten, but he never knew what I had. I'm being honest with you. Because I didn't feel bad. If he's gonna lose it to somebody, he might as well lose some to me.
Am I saying the wrong thing?
What kind of numbers did he do, can you remember?
